SESSIONAL/TERM WORK: Evaluation will consider progressive prototyping stages, successful integration of components, and design documentation. Students will produce an A4/A3 portfolio (printed) including design concepts, circuit diagrams, programming logic, fabrication details, and testing outcomes, along with the completed working prototype model. COURSE OUTCOMES: At the end of the course, the students are expected to 1. Apply advanced programming and electronics skills to control multiple components simultaneously. 2. Design and fabricate larger-scale kinetic or interactive systems. 3. Integrate hardware with computational design workflows for adaptive responses. 4. Test, refine, and present a fully functional prototype in a simulated or real environment.
